planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before transplanting; transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Paladin was among the first bell peppers bred with good resistance to Phytophthora blight, a devastating soil-borne disease that thrives in the wet, poorly drained conditions common after heavy Gulf South rain.

directions: Set out transplants in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date; Paladin was one of the first commercially significant bell pepper hybrids bred with meaningful resistance to Phytophthora blight, a fast-moving soil-borne disease that can wilt and kill an entire pepper planting within days after heavy rain leaves soil saturated, as commonly happens in Gulf Coast summer storms. It produces large, thick-walled, blocky green bells that ripen to red with good flavor and sweetness if left on the plant. Because good drainage alone cannot fully protect against Phytophthora in a wet season, Paladin's genetic resistance gives it a real advantage in low-lying or poorly drained garden beds. Harvest at the green stage for milder flavor or let fruit fully ripen to red, and keep picking regularly to encourage continued production.

common_name: Turnpike Bell Pepper (Broad-Spectrum Bacterial Spot-Resistant Hybrid)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before transplanting; transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Turnpike carries resistance to an unusually wide range of bacterial leaf spot races plus Phytophthora blight and tobacco mosaic virus, one of the broadest disease packages available in a bell pepper for humid, disease-heavy climates like the Gulf South.

directions: Set out transplants in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date; Turnpike is a bell pepper hybrid bred with resistance to a wide range of bacterial leaf spot races along with Phytophthora blight and tobacco mosaic virus, giving it one of the broadest disease packages available in a commercial bell pepper and making it especially well suited to the combination of heat, humidity, and rainfall pressure found across the Gulf South. It produces large, thick-walled, blocky green bells that ripen to red with good eating quality if left on the plant. Because it resists so many distinct disease pathogens at once, Turnpike tends to hold healthy foliage and continue setting fruit through conditions that would knock back less resistant varieties. Harvest at the green stage for milder flavor or let fruit fully ripen to red for maximum sweetness.

common_name: Alliance Bell Pepper (Multi-Virus and Bacterial Spot-Resistant Hybrid)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before transplanting; transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Alliance combines resistance to several races of bacterial leaf spot with tolerance to multiple viruses (potato virus Y, potato yellow mosaic virus, tobacco mosaic virus, and cucumber mosaic virus), an especially broad virus-resistance package for aphid-prone Gulf South gardens.

directions: Set out transplants in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date; Alliance is a bell pepper hybrid bred for resistance to several races of bacterial leaf spot along with tolerance to an unusually wide range of viruses, giving it strong protection against both the bacterial and viral diseases that spread readily through humid Gulf South gardens via rain splash and aphid activity. It produces large, thick-walled, blocky green bells that ripen to red with good flavor if left on the plant. Because viral diseases have no cure once a plant is infected, Alliance's broad tolerance package helps prevent the stunting, mottled foliage, and reduced yield that viruses cause in more susceptible varieties. Harvest at the green stage for milder flavor or let fruit fully ripen to red, and keep picking regularly to encourage continued fruit set.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before transplanting; transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Epic carries resistance to tobacco mosaic virus and is specifically recommended for Florida and Texas growing conditions, making it a solid choice for Gulf Coast eggplant growers.

directions: Set out transplants in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date, once nights stay reliably above 60°F; Epic is a vigorous, high-yielding hybrid eggplant carrying resistance to tobacco mosaic virus and is specifically recommended by Southern extension programs for Florida and Texas growing conditions. It produces large, classic glossy black-purple, oval fruit on a sturdy, well-branched plant that holds up well to summer heat. Harvest while the skin is still glossy and the fruit gives slightly to gentle pressure — dull skin and hard flesh signal overripe fruit with more seeds and a bitter edge. Keep picking regularly through the season to encourage continued flowering and fruit set, and provide consistent moisture, since eggplant grown under drought stress tends to develop tougher skin and more bitterness.
